title: Drafted in 1945 and re-upping after the war
summary: Drafted in January 1945 and trained as a surgical technician; after the war ended he re-upped for a year and went home on furlough.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Um, so, so through all this, what, what were you, so you're going through your schooling, uh, in the, in the 1930s, what, uh, I guess after high school, what, what, what were you thinking about, what were you going to do with your life? I mean, was there any thought issue growing up?

Nothing, nothing in particular that I knew that I wanted to do at that age. Uh, I had no idea what I wanted to do. Uh, I, as with any of my friends, none of us knew. We were just having fun and we were partying and, uh, hanging out. And, uh, when I was drafted into the service rather late, uh, January, uh, 10th, 1945. That's when you were drafted? That's when I was drafted. That's real life. Yes, really late. And, uh, went into the service and trained to be a surgical technician. Uh, and was about to, uh, uh, be shipped overseas to the, uh, uh, far east. Right. I was out in California. And since both wars were over by the time, when I went in, both wars were still on. But I remember I was on the, uh, uh, uh, rifle range and they said that, uh, Germany had surrendered. And then later on, it was around November, uh, prior to that, that, uh, Japan had surrendered. Okay. So what they told us in the army, since they didn't want to carry all that baggage around, uh, they said that if you wanted to re-enlist for a year, they would give you your must and out pay and you could go home for 30 days. So that was a great time. It was almost Christmas. So a bunch of us from New Orleans that were going to be shipped to the far east. We, uh, re-upped for the year, signed up for the year, got our must and out pay and came back to New Orleans for the holidays. Well, when I got back,
